problem: What is the first term of an arithmetic series if the common difference is $d=-4,$ and the sum of the first $20$ terms is ${S}_{20}=1\,160?$

feedback.problem: If the sum of the first $29$ terms of an arithmetic series is ${S}_{29}=319,$ and the common difference is $d=-3,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given the common difference of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=29$, $d=-3$, and ${S}_{N}=319$ into the formula above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}319 & =\frac{29}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(29-1)(-3)) \\ 638 & =29(2{a}_{1}-84) \\ 22 & =2{a}_{1}-84 \\ 106 & =2{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =53.\end{aligned}
$$
